repositories.brief_summary: Marshal and runtime_events overflow fixes merged, while Windows Unix.select and thread-starvation regressions were fixed and opened for review.
repositories.new_features_summary: Overflow fixes landed for Marshal unmarshaling and the runtime_events ring buffer, plus a new AI-assisted bug report guideline.
repositories.new_features:
- `Marshal.from_string`/`from_bytes` gained a guard against integer overflow when computing `header_len + data_len` from untrusted marshaled data, which could previously make bounds checks ineffective ([#15019](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15019)) by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy), reviewed by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) and [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA); validated with roughly 2 hours of AFL fuzzing that reproduced a crash on trunk and found none with the fix. The fix was also cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch and backported to 4.14 ([#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15030)).
- The `runtime_events` ring buffer's total size computation was changed from `int` to `size_t`, fixing an overflow that could `SIGBUS` the producer or silently write custom-event registrations through a truncated offset once the ring exceeded 2 GiB (`OCAMLRUNPARAM=e=21` and above) ([#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15000), fixes [#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), reviewed by [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj).
- `Utf8_lexeme` was extracted out of the `Misc` module into its own `utils/utf8_lexeme.ml(i)` files, so tools that vendor the parser no longer need to pull in all of `misc.ml` to get UTF-8 lexeme handling ([#15023](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15023)) by [Thomas Refis](https://github.com/trefis), reviewed by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- `AI.md` gained a new "Guidelines relevant to AI-assisted bug reports" section advising against mixing LLM-generated content into bug reports and cautioning about LLM-shrunk reproduction cases ([#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14899)) by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).
repositories.activity_summary: Windows regressions in Unix.select and thread scheduling were fixed, alongside POWER/arm64 codegen work and ongoing RFC discussions.
repositories.activity:
- Two Windows-specific bug fixes were opened and merged just after the week's end: a fix for `Unix.select` mapping polling results to the wrong file descriptor when a socket appears in multiple lists or a list has duplicates ([#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15025), fixes [#14758](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14758)), and a fix for a 5.5.0 regression where a thread that never yields starves other threads of its domain, caused by an invalid backup-thread handle after `CloseHandle` ([#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15029), fixes [#15028](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15028)) — both by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb), with the thread fix confirmed on Windows CI by [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz).
- POWER and arm64 codegen work continued: a fix for assembler errors when frame-management offsets exceed the 16-bit immediate field on POWER ([#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15021)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), and native rounding instructions for `Float.round`, `Float.trunc`, `ceil` and `floor` on arm64 and power ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) — both opened before and merged just after this week.
- `Format.flush_standard_formatters` was opened for changes to silence `Sys_error`, matching `Stdlib.flush_all`'s existing behaviour and fixing an uncaught exception at exit when stdout is a closed pipe ([#15026](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15026), fixes [#14765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14765)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), reviewed by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche).
- The GitHub issue template was updated to discourage posting AI-generated text in bug reports, linking to the new `AI.md` guidance ([#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15031)) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), following the discussion on [#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14899).
- `Int.popcount`, `leading_zeros` and `trailing_zeros` gained `%popcount`, `%clz` and `%ctz` primitives with arm64 code generation for `clz`/`ctz` (`popcount` stays a C call pending SIMD-only `cnt`), measured at roughly 2x faster for `leading_zeros`/`trailing_zeros` on an X-Gene ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15018), draft) opened by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham), building on the pure-OCaml versions added in [#14433](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14433).
- [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) opened a PR adding global-roots debugging support: an XOR-stamped pointer check plus a provenance skiplist recording where each root was registered, exposed through a new `ocaml roots` gdb command and a `Gc.check_roots` function, currently gated behind `DEBUG` ([#15027](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15027)).
- [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) opened a fix for the ocamldebug protocol clamping remote object headers to 32 bits, sending the full 64-bit header on request following [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy)'s suggestion ([#15022](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15022), fixes [#15012](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15012)).
- Ongoing `runtime_events` reliability work continued from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist): a consumer-side "corrupt stream" fix plus a producer-side memory-ordering fence addressing intermittent test-suite failures under small ring buffers ([#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016), fixes [#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)), and a proposal to widen the `lost_words` counter from `int` to `uint64_t` so it no longer wraps once more than 2^31 events are lost ([#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)).
- Longer-running proposals saw continued review: nested/inline record fields for record types ([#14527](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14527)) by [David Sancho](https://github.com/davesnx), the implicit source positions RFC ([#13886](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/13886)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), link-time linking ([#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14895)) by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust), and relocatable cross compilers ([#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14929)) by [@shym](https://github.com/shym).
repositories.discussions_summary: Maintainers pushed back on AI-generated content in issue threads, leading to a new guideline and issue-template change.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Repeated friction over LLM-generated content in issue reports: [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) asked whether [Nikos Gorogiannis](https://github.com/ngorogiannis)'s detailed runtime-event-spam report was LLM-drafted ([#15024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15024)), and [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz)'s thread-starvation report and follow-up comments ([#15028](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15028), [#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15029)) drew a direct request from [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) to stop posting raw LLM output, which fed into merging [#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14899) and the follow-up issue-template change ([#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15031)).
- On [#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14977), exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the interface, [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) discussed keeping the type abstract via a possible `[@@not_float]` attribute versus a `@deprecated`-field workaround that [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) proposed and [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) implemented.
- On [#15022](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15022), [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) and [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) discussed backward compatibility for the ocamldebug wire protocol and byte order for the new full-header encoding.
repositories.trends_summary: Runtime-events reliability, Windows regression fixes, and arm64/power codegen expansion were recurring themes this week.

- Architecture-specific codegen work kept expanding primitive support on arm64 and power, covering float rounding ([#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15017)), bit-counting primitives ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15018)), and a POWER assembler-offset fix ([#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15021)), largely from [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) and [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).

- Maintainers are actively formalizing pushback on AI-generated content in issue reports, via [AI.md](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14899) and the issue template change ([#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15031)).

repositories.brief_summary: Release-hardening work landed (reproducible Windows binaries, hardened sshpass retries) alongside a pinning-performance fix and a beta1 version bump.
repositories.new_features_summary: Reproducible Windows release binaries, a hardened release SSH helper, and a pinning scan performance fix for large projects.
repositories.new_features:
- **Reproducible Windows binaries**: the release Makefile now sets `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` and `LC_ALL=C`, and the release process gained a reproducibility check step, closing the long-standing [#6752](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6752) ([#7097](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7097) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- New `release/ssh-auto.sh` helper replaces raw `sshpass` calls in the release scripts with a retrying wrapper (`ssh-auto.sh password 240 ssh`), hardening the release pipeline against known `sshpass` instability ([#7096](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7096) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Pinning no longer recursively scans an entire project directory for `url`/`descr`/`files/**` adjacent files, cutting memory and time overhead on large projects when installing pinned packages ([#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101), fixes [#7098](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7098), by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Development version bumped to `2.6.0~beta1` in the install scripts, with SHA-512 checksums added for the beta1 binaries across Linux, macOS, BSD, and Windows targets ([shell/install.sh and shell/install.ps1](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/commit/d92bbf89424d5478c8decccd2ea64be671bfd70c))
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs targeted GC tuning, reftest ordering, opam-installer filtering, and `--no-lint`, while pinning scan and release-hardening PRs merged.
repositories.activity:
- Four **PRs opened** this week: a follow-up to stop scanning certain directories twice and avoid removal errors on non-existing directories during package removal by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#7106](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7106), queued on [#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101)), a proposed `opam install --no-lint` flag to suppress linting output ([#7111](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7111), fixes [#7110](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7110)), and a reftests change to make unordered test output reflect real, reproducible ordering rather than diff-minimising jumbled order ([#7107](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7107)), all by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- The **pinning scan** PR ([#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101)) went through detailed review by [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou), covering test-suite ordering, use of local archives instead of an HTTP server in tests, and linting behaviour during autopin, before being approved as ready to merge
- **Release hardening** completed with two merges by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate): the `sshpass`-retry wrapper ([#7096](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7096)) and the reproducible Windows build with a new reproducibility check step ([#7097](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7097), closing [#6752](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6752))
- Ongoing performance work on the `opam show`/cache path continued on [#7100](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7100) (making the GC work harder on low-end hardware instead of calling `Gc.compact`, fixes [#6521](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6521)), where [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) and [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) discussed `Marshal.from_channel` virtual-memory growth and `glibc` `malloc_trim` behaviour as contributing factors
- Other **carried-over open PRs** saw activity: disabling git's fsmonitor on opam-managed repositories with an implementation-approach suggestion from [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) ([#7090](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7090)), making a memoised mutable structure explicitly lazy ([#7088](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7088)), improving `OpamStd.Env.Name.{equal,compare}` performance on Windows to be allocation-free ([#7086](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7086)), and renaming/retyping the `translate`/`dir` argument of `OpamFilename.parse_patch` ([#7084](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7084)), all opened by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)
- An unrelated PR adding a Bun/TypeScript multi-agent framework was opened and closed the same day as out of scope for the repository ([#7102](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7102) by [Cazador0](https://github.com/Cazador0))
repositories.discussions_summary: Post-beta1 discussion on OpamFilename.in_dir removal and open questions on lint suppression and opam-installer section filtering.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) reported that `OpamFilename.in_dir`, used by the `orb` reproducible-build tool, was removed in the `2.6.0~beta1` release; [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) pointed to `OpamFilename.exec`/`OpamSystem.command` as replacements and gave a three-line reimplementation using `Unix.chdir` and `Fun.protect` ([#7103](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7103))
- Discussion on suppressing lint output beyond `opam show --no-lint` led to a plan to add the flag to `opam install` and related subcommands ([#7110](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7110), implemented in [#7111](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7111))

- [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) suggested removing opam's developer mode entirely in favour of a cache magic-version scheme that only changes on real marshalled-type changes, rather than merely disabling dev mode in reftests ([#7089](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7089), [#7104](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7104))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued focus on release-process reliability and reproducibility, plus memory/performance tuning around marshalling and directory scanning.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **Release-process reliability** is a recurring theme, with reproducible Windows binaries and retry-hardened SSH tooling merged this week ([#7096](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7096), [#7097](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7097)) following the `2.6.0~beta1` version bump
- **Memory and performance tuning** around marshalling and filesystem scanning continues across several open PRs, including GC behaviour under low memory limits ([#7100](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7100)), reduced directory scanning during pinning ([#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101), [#7106](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7106)), and allocation-free Windows environment comparisons ([#7086](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7086))
- **Test-suite determinism** is being tightened, with reftests moving away from unordered/jumbled diffs toward output that reflects real behaviour ([#7107](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7107)) and proposals to disable developer mode or rework cache versioning in tests ([#7089](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7089), [#7104](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7104))
- Nearly all substantive code and review activity this week came from a small, consistent group ([Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) and [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou)), consistent with prior weeks' pattern of concentrated maintenance

repositories.brief_summary: ocp-indent formatting support and on-type indentation landed alongside a run of LSP result-contract nullability fixes by Rudi Grinberg.
repositories.new_features_summary: Added ocp-indent as an alternative formatter and persistent on-type indentation via ocp-indent-rpc.
repositories.new_features:
- Added support for **ocp-indent** as an alternative document/range formatter by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg): formatter configuration is discovered by walking from the document's directory up to the workspace root, the closest `.ocamlformat` or `.ocp-indent` file wins, `.ocamlformat` takes precedence when both are present in the same directory, and the server falls back to an installed `ocp-indent` when neither is configured ([#2148](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2148), test coverage in [#2146](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2146))
- Implemented **`textDocument/onTypeFormatting`** for OCaml and ocamllex files by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), using a new optional, separately packaged `ocp-indent-rpc` helper process that is started lazily, negotiates a canonical S-expression protocol, is reused across requests, and caches resolved `.ocp-indent` configuration ([#1986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1986))
- Fixed **trailing newlines being dropped** from computed post-edit ranges, which previously caused replacement text ending in `\n` to leave the resulting range one line short, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2159](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2159), regression exposed in [#2158](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2158))
- Fixed **inlay hints leaking outside the requested range**, where Merlin could return hints positioned beyond the client's query range, by filtering converted hints before returning them, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2155](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2155), reproduction in [#2039](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2039))
- Fixed the **destruct code action applying offsets to the wrong line**, which could move an edit endpoint into the middle of a UTF-8 scalar or target unrelated source when Merlin's recovery location began on another line; the action now rejects unusable replies instead, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2063))

repositories.brief_summary: Sandboxing hardening landed behind Dune language 3.25/MDX 0.6, experimental FDO support was removed, and RPC/engine reliability fixes merged.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `dune trace cat` filters, sandboxed pkg-config/mdx/ppx-lint/ctypes actions gated to Dune lang 3.25, and removal of experimental FDO support.
repositories.new_features:
- New `--no-actions` and `--only-actions` flags for `dune trace cat` let users filter action events out of collected traces ([#16245](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16245), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- **Breaking change**: experimental OCamlFDO integration removed, including the `(fdo ...)` workspace field ([#16198](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16198), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Starting with **Dune language 3.25**, `pkg-config` queries are sandboxed so they cannot observe undeclared workspace inputs ([#16178](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16178), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)), PPX lint actions run sandboxed for the same reason ([#16176](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16176)), and cram test names keep their `.t` suffix, including aliases and `applies_to` ([#16146](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16146))
- From **MDX extension 0.6** (available with Dune 3.25), `ocaml-mdx dune-gen` generator actions ([#16177](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16177)) and `ocaml-mdx deps` dependency discovery ([#16183](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16183)) are now sandboxed
- Ctypes stub generation now runs sandboxed and honors its declared dependencies ([#16223](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16223)), and generated Ctypes helpers rebuild when headers from Ctypes' implicit include directories change ([#16243](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16243)), both by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Portable lock directories now select a single package version across all requested platforms and fail when no common version exists, fixing [#13647](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13647) ([#15982](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15982), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter))
- `Dune_action_plugin.V1.read_directory_with_glob` now returns an empty listing for absent directories instead of raising, fixing [#4445](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/4445) ([#16207](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16207), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- `$ dune rpc build` requests in watch mode now complete as soon as their own build finishes rather than waiting on unrelated concurrent RPC build requests, fixing the long-standing [#13788](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13788) ([#15191](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15191), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)); forwarded `build`/`runtest`/`exec` RPC paths are also now resolved relative to the client's directory instead of the server's ([#16267](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16267))
- Fixed rules with duplicate lock declarations deadlocking by acquiring each lock once ([#16252](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16252)), and prevented concurrent action children from closing shared redirections before siblings use them ([#16257](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16257)), both [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Fixed compiling Melange implementations of installed virtual libraries, with and without binary annotations, including transitive private module dependencies ([#16211](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16211), [#16212](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16212), [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro))
- Fixed missing Odoc generation for OxCaml parameter implementations ([#16200](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16200), [art-w](https://github.com/art-w))
- Preserved terminal output following malformed ANSI escape and erase-line sequences ([#16116](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16116)) and prevented diagnostic source locations at compact-position field boundaries from being truncated ([#16180](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16180)), both [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Series of **performance** changes switching `stdune` string scanning to `memchr` (string search, `split_on_char`, artifact and `dune subst` substitution scanning) and reducing allocations in string/path helpers ([#16224](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16224), [#16230](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16230), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)), plus marking blake3 `reset` as noalloc ([#16208](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16208))

- A coordinated **sandboxing hardening** sweep, almost entirely by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), gated behind `(lang dune 3.25)` or MDX 0.6, covering PPX lint actions, `pkg-config` queries, MDX generator/dependency actions, and Ctypes stub/link actions so these can no longer observe undeclared workspace inputs ([#16176](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16176), [#16177](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16177), [#16178](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16178), [#16183](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16183), [#16223](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16223), [#16243](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16243), [#16248](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16248))
- A **memchr-based performance** sweep across `stdune` string handling, `dune subst`, and artifact substitution scanning to cut allocations ([#16224](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16224), [#16230](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16230), [#16208](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16208))
- [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ran a long **refactor series** consolidating shared logic across the Melange, `js_of_ocaml`, opam, package, and preprocessing backends ahead of further Melange work ([#16147](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16147)-[#16165](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16165))
- A **design-first planning process** for package management: [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder)'s tool-implementation planning PR ([#16043](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16043)) spawned nine tracked design/implementation sub-issues for a new "discretionary tools" stanza feature ([#16185](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16185)-[#16196](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16196))
- **Backlog pruning**: [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) closed a cluster of long-dormant PRs dating back to late 2025/early 2026, inviting reopening once work resumes ([#12995](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/12995), [#12787](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/12787), [#11759](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/11759), [#11945](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/11945), [#13381](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13381), [#13324](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13324))

repositories.brief_summary: OxCaml mode-annotation rendering merged and a with-bounds crash fixed, continuing the broader effort to support OxCaml in odoc.
repositories.new_features_summary: Odoc now renders OxCaml mode annotations and fixes a with-bounds crash, plus a driver fix for stdlib detection in lib64.
repositories.new_features:
- Odoc now renders **OxCaml mode annotations** (e.g. `@ local`, `@ unique`, `@ once`) on values and arrow types, including heuristics ported from the OxCaml compiler to omit modes that are legacy, implied by other axes, or inferable from context, by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454), fixes [#1417](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1417))
- Fixed a crash (`Failure("invalid core type")`) when compiling documentation for packages such as `base` on OxCaml, caused by **with-bound expressions** referencing arbitrary types rather than only type variables, by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#1466](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1466), fixes [#1455](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1455))
- Updated compatibility for the **OxCaml 5.2.0minus39** compiler release, including a lower version bound in the opam files, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1469](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1469))
- Fixed `odoc_driver`'s **stdlib detection** to use Findlib's own logic and to accept `lib64/` install layouts (needed on openSUSE and similar distributions), by [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi) ([#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1474), fixes [#1477](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1477))
- `CHANGES.md` reorganized into **Added**/**Fixed** subsections and updated with entries for the merged OxCaml mode, with-bounds, and stdlib-detection work ([ea49422](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/commit/ea49422bf135a43c4ebfa08011255ff166997b6b))
repositories.activity_summary: Ongoing OxCaml support work continued with open PRs for kind abbreviations and include-functor rendering, plus dead-code cleanup.
repositories.activity:
- `include functor` support for OxCaml remains open with an active review discussion around desugaring the generated aliases, by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) with review input from [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) and [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- Support for rendering and linking **OxCaml kind abbreviations** is still under review, introducing a new namespace alongside types, with [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) flagging an issue with forward-reference resolution picking the wrong shadowed abbreviation, by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467), tracks [#1443](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1443))
- Removal of the unused `` `Forward `` constructor and related dead code in `xref2` remains an open draft, with [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) confirming several related code paths (`is_module_forward`, `UnresolvedForwardPath` guards) also look removable, by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1478](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1478))
- A simplification removing an unnecessary `id` wrapper optimisation was opened, reducing on-disk output size by around 30% and memory usage by around 5% with no measurable speed regression, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))
- A proposal to prefer `Stdlib` implementations over Odoc's own polyfills (following CI failures with `List.partition_map` on OCaml 4.11) was closed after [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) and [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) noted the risk of subtle semantic differences between custom and stdlib implementations, by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1476))
- The broader tracking issue for **OxCaml support** was updated as sub-issues for modes ([#1417](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1417)) and the with-bounds crash ([#1455](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1455)) were closed this week, by [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) ([#1411](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1411))
repositories.discussions_summary: Review discussion focused on how best to desugar include-functor output and on forward-reference resolution for kind abbreviations.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452), [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) prototyped an alternative "alias desugaring" approach for rendering `include functor`, questioning whether the current `DUMMY__` module approach correctly substitutes functor arguments, while agreeing the existing implementation is preferable to no support at all
- On [#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467), [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) raised a case where odoc's forward-reference resolution for kind abbreviations links to the wrong (later) definition when a name is shadowed within a signature
- On [#1476](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1476), [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) and [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) discussed the tradeoffs of relying on `Stdlib` polyfills versus maintaining Odoc's own implementations, concluding the PR's refactor wasn't worth the added uncertainty
repositories.trends_summary: OxCaml support continues as the dominant theme, moving from core rendering (modes) into edge cases and cleanup.
repositories.emerging_trends:

- Dead-code cleanup and simplification work is running alongside feature development, targeting the `` `Forward `` constructor ([#1478](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1478)) and the `id` wrapper optimisation ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))

repositories.brief_summary: Planet aggregator reliability work (timeouts, retries, dead-feed cleanup) alongside Dune 3.24.1 changelog and opam 2.5.2 announcement.
repositories.new_features_summary: Planet scraper gained retry/timeout/User-Agent handling and dead feed cleanup; Dune 3.24.1 changelog published.
repositories.new_features:
- Planet feed scraper now uses a 30s fetch timeout (up from river's hardcoded 3s), sends a descriptive `ocaml.org planet aggregator (+https://ocaml.org)` **User-Agent**, and retries failed fetches up to 3 times with exponential backoff (2s, 4s), reducing spurious scrape failures on slow or transiently-unreachable feeds, by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([#3752](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3752))
- Dead planet sources `ocaml-book` and `emilpriver` marked `disabled: true` in `data/planet-sources.yml` so they stop failing every nightly scrape while their already-archived posts stay published, by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([#3755](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3755), tracked in [#3753](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3753))
- `.gitignore` extended to cover stray OCaml build artifacts (`*.cmi`, `*.cmo`, `*.cmx`, `*.cmt`, `*.cmti`, `*.o`, `*.a`, `*.so`, `a.out`) left behind by ad-hoc `ocamlc`/`utop` runs outside `_build/`, while explicitly re-including the in-browser playground's tracked `playground/asset/stdlib/*.cmi` files, by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([#3757](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3757))
- Dune 3.24.1 platform release announcement and changelog added by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#3723](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3723))
- opam 2.5.2 release announcement added by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#3712](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3712))
- Automated OCaml Planet scrape runs added new posts including [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm)'s "Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days" and ".plan-26-34: Am I human or am I antibotty", plus the weekly OCaml Weekly News digest and a "Notes from week 34" post ([#3750](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3750), [#3751](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3751), [#3754](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3754))
repositories.activity_summary: Cuihtlauac Alvarado opened a repair-flag PR for the MirageOS feed that was superseded after upstream fixed the feed directly.

repositories.discussions_summary: Discussion on issue #3753 resolved the status of five failing planet feeds through direct author replies.

repositories.trends_summary: Continued focus on OCaml Planet aggregator robustness, favoring opt-in per-source fixes over global changes.
repositories.emerging_trends:

repositories.new_features_summary: Node runtime now locates `.wasm` assets relative to the runtime file instead of the process entry point.
repositories.new_features:
- Fixed **Wasm asset resolution** in the Node runtime: `.wasm` files are now located relative to `module.filename` instead of `require.main.filename`, so programs loaded via `require` (e.g. behind a CLI wrapper), through a symlink, or from worker threads/`node -e` (where `require.main` is undefined) can find their assets; the same fix applies to the WASI runtime ([#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2389))
- Documentation build now fails on a dead reference or a leftover wiki image, via a new `--strict-refs` flag on `wodoc build` in the dev doc-build CI job, guarding against regressions like broken tutorial screenshots or dead intra-manual links ([#2411](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2411))
repositories.activity_summary: Seven new PRs opened around Wasm sourcemaps, typed arrays, BOM handling and CI, while large Web API binding PRs and a single-linear-memory change stayed under review.
repositories.activity:
- Seven PRs were opened and remain unmerged: [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) fixed sourcemap-support detection on Windows where the Binaryen version probe silently disabled sourcemaps because it redirected stderr to the non-existent `/dev/null` ([#2418](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2418)), added a sourcemap mapping at the start of every function ([#2417](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2417)), preserved leading BOMs when converting OCaml strings to JavaScript strings by using `ignoreBOM:true` with `TextDecoder` ([#2414](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2414)), added a `--setenv` flag to `wasm_of_ocaml` ([#2415](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2415)), fixed typed array constructors to take a `number_t js_array t` rather than a `float js_array t` ([#2416](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2416)), and opened draft PRs to run the test suites under bun in CI ([#2413](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2413)) and to benchmark number unboxing and integer optimizations ([#2410](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2410))
- [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) continued work on consolidating the Wasm runtime to a **single linear memory**, merging the separate memories used by the `caml_buffer` scratch buffer, the zstd and blake2 implementations, and the WASI libc, since Safari does not support modules with multiple memories ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405))
- [Hugo Heuzard](https://github.com/hhugo) has two large Claude-Code-assisted binding PRs pending review: `BroadcastChannel` and `SharedWorker` bindings filling Tier 2 communication gaps from `API-STATUS.md` ([#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400)), and Web Audio plus Media Capture bindings alongside a completed `Dom_html.mediaElement` binding ([#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401))

- **Wasm-of-ocaml maturation** continues to be the dominant theme, covering sourcemap correctness on Windows and per-function granularity ([#2418](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2418), [#2417](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2417)), consolidating to a single linear memory for Safari compatibility ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405)), and fixing Node asset/module resolution ([#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2389))
- Several PRs are tagged **`🤖 Generated with Claude Code`**, including the large Web API binding additions and the stdlib snapshot refresh ([#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400), [#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401), [#2412](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2412)), suggesting increasing use of AI-assisted contributions for binding coverage and test maintenance
- Continued expansion of **browser/Web API binding coverage** tracked against `API-STATUS.md`, filling Tier 2 gaps for communication (`BroadcastChannel`, `SharedWorker`) and media (Web Audio, Media Capture) APIs ([#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400), [#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401))
repositories.contributors_summary: Three contributors were active: Jérôme Vouillon on Wasm runtime and sourcemap fixes, Hugo Heuzard on Web API bindings and CI test maintenance, and Vincent Balat on documentation build tooling.
repositories.contributors:
- [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) merged the Wasm asset resolution fix ([#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2389)) and opened six further PRs covering Windows sourcemap detection ([#2418](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2418)), per-function sourcemap mappings ([#2417](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2417)), BOM preservation in string conversion ([#2414](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2414)), a `wasm_of_ocaml --setenv` flag ([#2415](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2415)), a typed array constructor fix ([#2416](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2416)), and draft PRs for running tests under bun ([#2413](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2413)) and benchmarking number unboxing ([#2410](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2410)), plus ongoing work consolidating the Wasm runtime to a single linear memory ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405))
- [Hugo Heuzard](https://github.com/hhugo) merged a stdlib 5.6 test-snapshot refresh to fix a CI failure caused by OCaml trunk changes ([#2412](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2412)) and has two large binding PRs open for review, adding BroadcastChannel/SharedWorker bindings ([#2400](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2400)) and Web Audio/Media Capture bindings ([#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401))
- [Vincent Balat](https://github.com/balat) added a documentation CI check that fails the build on dead references or leftover wiki images, and responded to review feedback from [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) about viewing the CI log ([#2411](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2411))
- [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) commented on the JS output size issue, asking whether `ppx_module_timer` contributes to unnecessary bundle size ([#812](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/812))

repositories.brief_summary: New atomic idx_atomic operations and a CFG block-layout pass landed alongside continued mode-system and DWARF-debug-info work.
repositories.new_features_summary: New idx_atomic operations, addressable kinds, a -cfg-block-layout flag, mixed-block recursion, and AST-editing compiler hooks.
repositories.new_features:
- New atomic operations (`exchange`, `compare_and_set`, `compare_exchange`, `fetch_and_add`, `add`, `sub`, `logand`, and more) added to `Stdlib_stable.Idx_atomic`, implementing the previously-missing `idx_atomic` primitives by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([#6743](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6743)), building on a cleanup of the `%atomic_load_idx`/`%atomic_set_idx` lowering ([#6746](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6746))
- New `-cfg-block-layout` compiler flag adding a static CFG block-layout optimization pass by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#6918](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6918))
- Recursive uses are now permitted within non-value fields of mixed blocks, relaxing a restriction for **unboxed types** code by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6847](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6847))
- **Parsetree compiler hooks** can now edit the AST, letting external tooling transform the parse tree before typing runs, by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6826](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6826))
- Mode-implication inference improved for functor arguments/returns and external declarations by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([#6745](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6745))
- Continued build-out of the **mode-variable-levels** infrastructure covering update-level, generalize, copy, locality `alloc_mode`, and comonadic curry mode by [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) ([#5478](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5478), [#6966](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6966))
- Fixed a memory leak from tail-calling a local-returning function by [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) ([#6396](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6396))
- Fixed continuations being invoked with invalid kinds in `from_lambda`, a **Flambda2** bug, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6291](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6291))
- Fixed young effect handlers being forgotten between `update`/`continue` by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6768](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6768))
- Reduced `CAML_GC_MESSAGE` overhead and many-domain CPU overhead by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6888](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6888)), plus smaller minor-GC tables and a simplified "reserve" algorithm ([#6840](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6840))
- Faster compilation of `encode_instruction.ml` by flipping a match's argument order by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([#6936](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6936))
- Fixed caching of DWARF type DIEs, cutting redundant debug-info generation, by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6916](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6916)), and DIEs for the immediate-or-pointer discriminant enum are now shared per compilation unit ([#6945](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6945))
- Fixed incorrect DWARF file paths by [Kevin Svetlitski](https://github.com/Svetlitski) ([#6882](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6882))
- Documentation for **mode implications** rewritten to distinguish "fixed" sites (where every axis must be pinned) from "flexible" sites (where only written axes are constrained), alongside the inference fix by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([#6745](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6745))
repositories.activity_summary: Many open PRs advanced Merlin-diagnostics import, DWARF-5 support, link-time optimization, and the parameterized-libraries (functorize) effort.
repositories.activity:

- [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) opened a run of **DWARF-5** PRs including base-address/offset-pair location and range lists ([#6926](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6926)), LLDB DWARF-5 test variants ([#6957](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6957)), a selectable `-gdwarf-version` flag ([#6923](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6923)), optional DWARF-4 type units in `.debug_types` ([#6920](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6920)), and enabling `--enable-oxcaml-dwarf-on-compiler` by default ([#6911](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6911)), plus a fix for `unit#` and unboxed-type DWARF shapes ([#6969](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6969))

- [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) opened several **functorize**/parameterized-libraries PRs deriving block formats from `.cmi` coercions, fixing argument-block projection on mixed module blocks, and checking `arg_param` during projection ([#6917](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6917), [#6912](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6912), [#6925](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6925), [#6924](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6924)), plus lazy loading of hidden manifests in the load path ([#6951](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6951)) and a magic-number bump for ox6 that merged this week ([#6906](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6906))

repositories.discussions_summary: Design discussions centered on addressable/mode kinds, module-alias signature semantics, and DWARF location-list encoding.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Extended review discussion on **Addressable kinds** between [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) and [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) covering the `Le_result` design and `constrain_*_addressable` helpers, working through several rounds to keep the core lattice logic clean ([#6712](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6712))

- Detailed review threads on exposing module-type information for compiler artifacts and a new `module-type-impls` query, both opened by [Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy) as part of the Merlin-integration effort ([#6801](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6801), [#6811](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6811))

repositories.brief_summary: Eio landed a new documentation index page and reviewed proposals for chown id validation and a concurrent partition_map helper.
repositories.new_features_summary: A curated `index.mld` landing page for the Eio API docs was merged, replacing the default auto-generated index.
repositories.new_features: - Added a hand-written documentation index page for the `Eio` library that groups the API by purpose (fibers/switches/cancellation, host resources, files, networking, time, concurrency primitives, collections, domains, exceptions, and private/backend-only modules) rather than relying on the default auto-generated odoc index, merged by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926))
repositories.activity_summary: Two PRs remained open under review: an out-of-range chown id check and a fiber-based `partition_map` whose concurrency implementation was questioned.
repositories.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a PR to reject out-of-range `chown` uid/gid values in `eio_unix` while still allowing `-1` to mean "leave unchanged", per POSIX semantics ([#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928)); [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) questioned whether the kernel already validates this and pointed out that `uid_t` is unsigned on Linux, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) argued a portable-layer check is still prudent since the signedness of `uid_t`/`gid_t` varies across platforms, citing [python/cpython#46289](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/46289)
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)'s proposal to add `Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map` remained open for review ([#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927)); both [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) noted the fork-then-immediately-wait pattern in the initial implementation was not actually running concurrently, and suggested starting instead with a simpler one-liner built on the existing `map` function, optimizing later only if fiber-creation overhead proves to be a bottleneck
- The new `index.mld` landing page for the API reference was merged this week after review, replacing the default generated index with a curated, purpose-grouped layout ([#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926))
repositories.discussions_summary: Reviewers scrutinized whether a proposed `partition_map` helper truly runs fibers concurrently and whether portable chown validation duplicates kernel checks.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) identified that forking a fiber and immediately waiting on it does not provide real concurrency, using the test output as evidence, and recommended a simpler `List.partition_map Fun.id (map ?max_fibers fn items)` implementation as a starting point
- On [#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928), [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) raised whether kernel-side checks make an explicit uid/gid range check redundant and noted `uid_t`'s unsigned representation on Linux, prompting [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) to explain the cross-platform signedness rationale for validating in the portable layer, drawing a parallel to [python/cpython#46289](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/46289)
repositories.trends_summary: Code review this week centered on verifying real concurrency behavior and cross-platform correctness rather than just API surface.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Reviewers are pushing back on complexity in new concurrency helpers, preferring simple compositions of existing primitives (e.g. building `partition_map` from `map`) unless a performance need is demonstrated ([#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
- Continued attention to portability edge cases in the `eio_unix` POSIX bindings, including signedness differences in system types across platforms ([#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928))
- Investment in documentation discoverability continued with a curated API index replacing auto-generated docs ([#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926))
repositories.contributors_summary: Three contributors were active: one opened a new API proposal, one opened a portability fix, and one merged a documentation improvement while both reviewed each other's work.
repositories.contributors:
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura) proposed adding `Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map` and received review feedback on its concurrency implementation ([#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a PR to validate `chown` uid/gid ranges while allowing `-1` for "unchanged" ([#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928)), and reviewed [#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927), flagging that its fiber-forking approach did not achieve real concurrency and suggesting a simpler one-liner alternative
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) merged the new documentation index page ([#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926)) and reviewed both open PRs, questioning the concurrency claims in [#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927) and the necessity of an extra kernel-level check in [#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928)

group_summaries.brief_summary: Dune shipped a sandboxing hardening sweep and RPC fixes, ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent support, and opam/odoc landed release and OxCaml fixes.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Dune sandboxed build actions under lang 3.25; ocaml-lsp added ocp-indent formatting; opam shipped reproducible Windows builds; odoc rendered OxCaml modes.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **ocaml/dune** gated a sandboxing hardening sweep behind **Dune language 3.25**/MDX 0.6, covering `pkg-config` queries ([ocaml/dune#16178](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16178)), PPX lint actions ([ocaml/dune#16176](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16176)), MDX generator/dependency actions ([ocaml/dune#16177](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16177), [ocaml/dune#16183](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16183)), and Ctypes stub/link actions ([ocaml/dune#16223](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16223), [ocaml/dune#16243](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16243)); it also removed the experimental `(fdo ...)` OCamlFDO integration as a **breaking change** ([ocaml/dune#16198](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16198)), fixed RPC `build` requests in watch mode to no longer wait on unrelated concurrent builds ([ocaml/dune#15191](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15191)), and made portable lock directories select a single package version across all requested platforms ([ocaml/dune#15982](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15982)), all mostly by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- **ocaml/ocaml-lsp** added **ocp-indent** as an alternative document/range formatter with config auto-discovery ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2148](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2148)) and implemented `textDocument/onTypeFormatting` via a new `ocp-indent-rpc` helper process ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1986)), both by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- **ocaml/opam** merged **reproducible Windows release binaries** with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0`/`LC_ALL=C` and a reproducibility check step, closing [ocaml/opam#6752](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6752) ([ocaml/opam#7097](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7097)), a hardened `release/ssh-auto.sh` retry wrapper replacing raw `sshpass` calls ([ocaml/opam#7096](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7096)), and a pinning-scan performance fix that avoids recursively scanning entire project directories ([ocaml/opam#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101)), all by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate); the dev version was bumped to **2.6.0~beta1**
- **ocaml/odoc** now renders **OxCaml mode annotations** (`@ local`, `@ unique`, `@ once`) on values and arrow types ([ocaml/odoc#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454)) and fixed a crash compiling docs for packages like `base` on OxCaml caused by with-bound expressions referencing arbitrary types ([ocaml/odoc#1466](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1466)), both by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w); `odoc_driver`'s stdlib detection was fixed to support `lib64/` install layouts ([ocaml/odoc#1474](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1474) by [@katrinafyi](https://github.com/katrinafyi))
- **ocsigen/js_of_ocaml** fixed **Wasm asset resolution** in the Node runtime to locate `.wasm` files relative to `module.filename` instead of `require.main.filename`, fixing lookups behind CLI wrappers, symlinks, and worker threads ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2389) by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon))

group_summaries.brief_summary: oxcaml/oxcaml added idx_atomic ops and a CFG block-layout pass while advancing mode-system, DWARF-5, and in-tree Merlin integration work.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: New idx_atomic operations, addressable kinds, a -cfg-block-layout flag, mixed-block recursion, and AST-editing compiler hooks.
group_summaries.new_features:
- New atomic operations (`exchange`, `compare_and_set`, `compare_exchange`, `fetch_and_add`, `add`, `sub`, `logand`, and more) added to `Stdlib_stable.Idx_atomic`, implementing the previously-missing `idx_atomic` primitives by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6743](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6743)), building on a cleanup of the `%atomic_load_idx`/`%atomic_set_idx` lowering ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6746](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6746))
- New `-cfg-block-layout` compiler flag adding a static CFG block-layout optimization pass by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6918](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6918))
- Recursive uses are now permitted within non-value fields of mixed blocks, relaxing a restriction for **unboxed types** code by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6847](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6847))
- **Parsetree compiler hooks** can now edit the AST, letting external tooling transform the parse tree before typing runs, by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6826](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6826))
- Mode-implication inference improved for functor arguments/returns and external declarations by [@dkalinichenko-js](https://github.com/dkalinichenko-js) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6745](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6745))
- Continued build-out of the **mode-variable-levels** infrastructure covering update-level, generalize, copy, locality `alloc_mode`, and comonadic curry mode by [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#5478](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5478), [oxcaml/oxcaml#6966](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6966))
- Fixed a memory leak from tail-calling a local-returning function by [@ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6396](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6396))
- Fixed continuations being invoked with invalid kinds in `from_lambda`, a **Flambda2** bug, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6291](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6291))
- Fixed young effect handlers being forgotten between `update`/`continue` by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6768](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6768))

group_summaries.new_features_summary: Overflow fixes landed for Marshal unmarshaling and the runtime_events ring buffer, plus a new AI-assisted bug report guideline.
group_summaries.new_features:
- `Marshal.from_string`/`from_bytes` gained a guard against integer overflow when computing `header_len + data_len` from untrusted marshaled data, which could previously make bounds checks ineffective ([ocaml/ocaml#15019](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15019)) by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy), reviewed by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) and [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA); validated with roughly 2 hours of AFL fuzzing that reproduced a crash on trunk and found none with the fix. The fix was also cherry-picked to the 5.5 branch and backported to 4.14 ([ocaml/ocaml#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15030)).
- The `runtime_events` ring buffer's total size computation was changed from `int` to `size_t`, fixing an overflow that could `SIGBUS` the producer or silently write custom-event registrations through a truncated offset once the ring exceeded 2 GiB (`OCAMLRUNPARAM=e=21` and above) ([ocaml/ocaml#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#14999](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14999)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), reviewed by [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj).
- `Utf8_lexeme` was extracted out of the `Misc` module into its own `utils/utf8_lexeme.ml(i)` files, so tools that vendor the parser no longer need to pull in all of `misc.ml` to get UTF-8 lexeme handling ([ocaml/ocaml#15023](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15023)) by [Thomas Refis](https://github.com/trefis), reviewed by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- `AI.md` gained a new "Guidelines relevant to AI-assisted bug reports" section advising against mixing LLM-generated content into bug reports and cautioning about LLM-shrunk reproduction cases ([ocaml/ocaml#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14899)) by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).

group_summaries.activity_summary: Windows regressions in Unix.select and thread scheduling were fixed, alongside POWER/arm64 codegen work; ocaml/RFCs had no activity.
group_summaries.activity:
- Two Windows-specific bug fixes were opened and merged just after the week's end: a fix for `Unix.select` mapping polling results to the wrong file descriptor when a socket appears in multiple lists or a list has duplicates ([ocaml/ocaml#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15025), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#14758](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14758)), and a fix for a 5.5.0 regression where a thread that never yields starves other threads of its domain, caused by an invalid backup-thread handle after `CloseHandle` ([ocaml/ocaml#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#15028](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15028)) — both by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb), with the thread fix confirmed on Windows CI by [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz).
- POWER and arm64 codegen work continued: a fix for assembler errors when frame-management offsets exceed the 16-bit immediate field on POWER ([ocaml/ocaml#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15021)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), and native rounding instructions for `Float.round`, `Float.trunc`, `ceil` and `floor` on arm64 and power ([ocaml/ocaml#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15017)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) — both opened before and merged just after this week.
- `Format.flush_standard_formatters` was opened for changes to silence `Sys_error`, matching `Stdlib.flush_all`'s existing behaviour and fixing an uncaught exception at exit when stdout is a closed pipe ([ocaml/ocaml#15026](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15026), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#14765](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14765)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), reviewed by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche).
- The GitHub issue template was updated to discourage posting AI-generated text in bug reports, linking to the new `AI.md` guidance ([ocaml/ocaml#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15031)) by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), following the discussion on [ocaml/ocaml#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14899).
- `Int.popcount`, `leading_zeros` and `trailing_zeros` gained `%popcount`, `%clz` and `%ctz` primitives with arm64 code generation for `clz`/`ctz` (`popcount` stays a C call pending SIMD-only `cnt`), measured at roughly 2x faster for `leading_zeros`/`trailing_zeros` on an X-Gene ([ocaml/ocaml#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15018), draft) opened by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham), building on the pure-OCaml versions added in [ocaml/ocaml#14433](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14433).
- [Romain Beauxis](https://github.com/toots) opened a PR adding global-roots debugging support: an XOR-stamped pointer check plus a provenance skiplist recording where each root was registered, exposed through a new `ocaml roots` gdb command and a `Gc.check_roots` function, currently gated behind `DEBUG` ([ocaml/ocaml#15027](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15027)).
- [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) opened a fix for the ocamldebug protocol clamping remote object headers to 32 bits, sending the full 64-bit header on request following [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy)'s suggestion ([ocaml/ocaml#15022](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15022), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#15012](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15012)).
- Ongoing `runtime_events` reliability work continued from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist): a consumer-side "corrupt stream" fix plus a producer-side memory-ordering fence addressing intermittent test-suite failures under small ring buffers ([ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15016), fixes [ocaml/ocaml#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)), and a proposal to widen the `lost_words` counter from `int` to `uint64_t` so it no longer wraps once more than 2^31 events are lost ([ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15010)).
- Longer-running proposals saw continued review: nested/inline record fields for record types ([ocaml/ocaml#14527](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14527)) by [David Sancho](https://github.com/davesnx), the implicit source positions RFC ([ocaml/ocaml#13886](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13886)) by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), link-time linking ([ocaml/ocaml#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14895)) by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust), and relocatable cross compilers ([ocaml/ocaml#14929](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14929)) by [@shym](https://github.com/shym).
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- Repeated friction over LLM-generated content in issue reports: [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) asked whether [Nikos Gorogiannis](https://github.com/ngorogiannis)'s detailed runtime-event-spam report was LLM-drafted ([ocaml/ocaml#15024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15024)), and [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz)'s thread-starvation report and follow-up comments ([ocaml/ocaml#15028](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15028), [ocaml/ocaml#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029)) drew a direct request from [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) to stop posting raw LLM output, which fed into merging [ocaml/ocaml#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14899) and the follow-up issue-template change ([ocaml/ocaml#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15031)).
- On [ocaml/ocaml#14977](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14977), exposing that `Atomic.t` is not a float in the interface, [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) and [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) discussed keeping the type abstract via a possible `[@@not_float]` attribute versus a `@deprecated`-field workaround that [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) proposed and [Török Edwin](https://github.com/edwintorok) implemented.
- On [ocaml/ocaml#15022](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15022), [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) and [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls) discussed backward compatibility for the ocamldebug wire protocol and byte order for the new full-header encoding.
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Runtime-events reliability received sustained attention, with overflow and corruption fixes/proposals spanning this week and last ([ocaml/ocaml#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000), [ocaml/ocaml#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15016), [ocaml/ocaml#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15010)) plus a new spam report ([ocaml/ocaml#15024](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15024)), mostly driven by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- Architecture-specific codegen work kept expanding primitive support on arm64 and power, covering float rounding ([ocaml/ocaml#15017](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15017)), bit-counting primitives ([ocaml/ocaml#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15018)), and a POWER assembler-offset fix ([ocaml/ocaml#15021](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15021)), largely from [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) and [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- Windows support saw two distinct regression fixes land for `Unix.select` ([ocaml/ocaml#15025](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15025)) and thread scheduling ([ocaml/ocaml#15029](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15029)), both from [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- Maintainers are actively formalizing pushback on AI-generated content in issue reports, via the new `AI.md` guidelines ([ocaml/ocaml#14899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14899)) and the issue template change ([ocaml/ocaml#15031](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15031)).

- Two eio PRs remained open under review: a `chown` uid/gid range check ([ocaml-multicore/eio#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928)) and a `Fiber.List.partition_map` proposal whose concurrency implementation was questioned ([ocaml-multicore/eio#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
group_summaries.activity_summary: Two eio PRs stayed open under review: a portable chown uid/gid validation and a fiber-based partition_map whose concurrency was disputed.
group_summaries.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened a PR to reject out-of-range `chown` uid/gid values in `eio_unix` while still allowing `-1` to mean "leave unchanged", per POSIX semantics ([ocaml-multicore/eio#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928)); [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) questioned whether the kernel already validates this and noted `uid_t` is unsigned on Linux, and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) argued a portable-layer check is still prudent given `uid_t`/`gid_t` signedness varies across platforms, citing [python/cpython#46289](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/46289)
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)'s proposal to add `Eio.Fiber.List.partition_map` to [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) remained open for review ([ocaml-multicore/eio#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927)); [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) noted the fork-then-immediately-wait pattern in the initial implementation was not actually concurrent, and suggested a simpler one-liner built on the existing `map` function instead
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- On [ocaml-multicore/eio#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) identified that forking a fiber and immediately waiting on it does not provide real concurrency, using the test output as evidence, and recommended a simpler `List.partition_map Fun.id (map ?max_fibers fn items)` implementation as a starting point
- On [ocaml-multicore/eio#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928), [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) raised whether kernel-side checks make an explicit uid/gid range check redundant and noted `uid_t`'s unsigned representation on Linux, prompting [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) to explain the cross-platform signedness rationale for validating in the portable layer, drawing a parallel to [python/cpython#46289](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/46289)
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- Reviewers in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) are pushing back on complexity in new concurrency helpers, preferring simple compositions of existing primitives (e.g. building `partition_map` from `map`) unless a performance need is demonstrated ([ocaml-multicore/eio#927](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/927))
- Continued attention to portability edge cases in the `eio_unix` POSIX bindings, including signedness differences in system types across platforms ([ocaml-multicore/eio#928](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/928))
- Investment in documentation discoverability continued in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) with a curated API index replacing auto-generated docs ([ocaml-multicore/eio#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926))
- Eight of the nine group repositories recorded no activity this week, concentrating all visible work in [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio)

weekly_summary.brief_summary: Core fixed Marshal/runtime_events overflow bugs, OxCaml added idx_atomic ops, and tools shipped dune sandboxing hardening plus opam 2.6.0~beta1.
weekly_summary.new_features_summary: Marshal/runtime_events overflow fixes, OxCaml idx_atomic ops, dune sandboxing under lang 3.25, ocp-indent in ocaml-lsp, opam 2.6.0~beta1.
weekly_summary.new_features:
- __RUMINANT:core__ [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml) closed an integer-overflow hole in `Marshal.from_string`/`from_bytes`'s bounds check on untrusted data, validated with AFL fuzzing and backported to the 5.5 branch and 4.14 ([ocaml/ocaml#15019](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15019), [ocaml/ocaml#15030](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15030)) by [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy).
- __RUMINANT:core__ [ocaml/ocaml](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml) widened the `runtime_events` ring buffer's size computation from `int` to `size_t`, fixing a `SIGBUS`/truncated-offset bug once the ring exceeds 2 GiB ([ocaml/ocaml#15000](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15000)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ [oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml) added new **`Idx_atomic`** operations (`exchange`, `compare_and_set`, `fetch_and_add`, and more) implementing the previously-missing `idx_atomic` primitives, by [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6743](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6743)).
- __RUMINANT:oxcaml__ [oxcaml/oxcaml](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml) added a new `-cfg-block-layout` compiler flag for static CFG block-layout optimization, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6918](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6918)), and **parsetree compiler hooks** that let external tooling edit the AST before typing, by [Stephen Dolan](https://github.com/stedolan) ([oxcaml/oxcaml#6826](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6826)).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune) gated a **sandboxing hardening sweep** behind Dune language 3.25/MDX 0.6, covering `pkg-config`, PPX lint, MDX, and Ctypes actions ([ocaml/dune#16178](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16178), [ocaml/dune#16176](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16176), [ocaml/dune#16223](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16223)), and removed the experimental `(fdo ...)` OCamlFDO integration as a **breaking change** ([ocaml/dune#16198](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16198)), mostly by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp) added **ocp-indent** as an alternative document/range formatter with config auto-discovery and `textDocument/onTypeFormatting` support via a new `ocp-indent-rpc` helper, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#2148](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/2148), [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1986)).
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam) merged **reproducible Windows release binaries** (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0`/`LC_ALL=C`) and a pinning-scan performance fix that avoids recursively scanning entire project directories, by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([ocaml/opam#7097](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7097), [ocaml/opam#7101](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7101)); the dev version was bumped to **2.6.0~beta1**.
- __RUMINANT:tools__ [ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc) now renders **OxCaml mode annotations** (`@ local`, `@ unique`, `@ once`) on values and arrow types, and fixed a crash compiling docs for packages like `base` on OxCaml, both by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([ocaml/odoc#1454](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1454), [ocaml/odoc#1466](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1466)).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ [ocaml/opam-repository](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository) published **opam 2.6.0~beta1** as eight packages by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30542](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30542)), alongside **mirage-crypto 2.4.1** (CCM/RSA/poly1305 fixes) and a coordinated **Miou/mnet/Solo5** unikernel-stack release, all by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) and [Calascibetta Romain](https://github.com/dinosaure) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30568](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30568), [ocaml/opam-repository#30582](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30582), [ocaml/opam-repository#30581](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30581)).
- __RUMINANT:multicore__ [ocaml-multicore/eio](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio) merged a hand-written `index.mld` documentation landing page grouping the API by purpose, replacing the auto-generated odoc index, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([ocaml-multicore/eio#926](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/926)).
- __RUMINANT:ecosystem__ [ocaml/ocaml.org](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org) hardened the planet feed scraper with a 30s fetch timeout (up from 3s), a descriptive User-Agent, and retries with exponential backoff, by [Cuihtlauac Alvarado](https://github.com/cuihtlauac) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3752](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3752)); its weekly automated scraper build also published a new `scraper-latest` release ([ocaml/ocaml.org releases](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/releases/tag/scraper-latest)).
